messages:
maya: heads up — i'm kicking off a proposal to move from per-route timebucket rows to a tenant-scoped metric-bucket model for console telemetry. goal is to avoid hot-route shards and simplify per-tenant retention/quotas.

alex: curious about the data shape change. is this a new PK or just a clustering/index change?

maya: new PK. previously we had (route_id, day, metric) -> value. new shape will be (tenant_id, metric_bucket, day) with a mapping from route -> bucket. buckets are small (~8-16 routes) hashed per tenant to spread load.

devin: how will dashboards query for single-route time series? will we need a join on the route->bucket map? that could be annoying for p99s.

maya: plan: read adapter will expose the old API. two strategies: 1) read-time expansion (adapter fetches bucket and filters client-side), 2) materialized per-route view for top-n routes only. prefer (1) for now, (2) later for perf-critical routes.

alex: can we see a backfill plan? also worried about index rebuild time on main analytics cluster.

maya: backfill outline in brief:
```
ALTER TABLE telemetry ADD COLUMN metric_bucket bigint;
-- compute bucket: hash(tenant_id || route_id) % N
UPDATE telemetry SET metric_bucket = compute_bucket(tenant_id, route_id) WHERE metric_bucket IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX ON telemetry (tenant_id, metric_bucket, day);
```
We'll run shadow writes for 2 weeks, then cut reads.

sarah: shadow write + dualread makes sense. we should also add a feature-flagged canary: send read traffic for 1% of tenants through adapter to validate correctness and latency.

devin: +1 but add a telemetry sanity check job that compares sums between old and new shape daily for canary tenants. log diffs > 0.5% as alerts.

maya: agreed. i'll draft the canary checklist:
- dualwrite enabled for all writes (old and new)
- backfill job with rate-limit to avoid OOMs
- read adapter deployed behind ff: canary tenants -> adapter, others -> old path
- daily reconciliation job with slack alerts

alex: what about query planning? for example console expects p50/p95 queries across tens of thousands of routes. adapter needs to be efficient for aggregation across buckets.

maya: adapter will pre-aggregate per-bucket time series and expose selective route unroll only when requested. for overview dashboards we return tenant-level aggregates quickly. detailed per-route drilldowns will trigger the more expensive expansion.

sarah: rollout UX: ops needs a toggle to pin tenants to old/new behavior and a safety rollback that switches reads instantly. also expose status per-tenant in console (backfill progress, last-consistency-check).

devin: DB ops: we should schedule index create concurrently and with small batch backfill. also consider rewriting the ingestion pipeline to emit metric_bucket at source to avoid heavy UPDATEs.

maya: yes — plan is to push compute to ingest side in two phases: 1) backfill from SQL job, 2) change ingest lambda to write metric_bucket so new rows are correct. this reduces long-running UPDATEs.

alex: any storage/perf tradeoffs? buckets reduce cardinality for hot-tenant scans but increase per-row ambiguity. also retention TTL per-tenant now easier, so we can GC faster for some customers.

maya: correct. we expect net storage decrease due to consolidated index sizes and fewer hot duplicates. still need to validate with a small-scale synthetic workload.

iris-bot: migration-job/schedule created: telemetry.bucketization.backfill v1 -> queued for 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC (owner: maya).

sarah: assign owners & runbook please. can we add a quick playbook: how to detect mis-bucketed routes (hash drift), and how to reassign buckets?

maya: will add playbook. short version: rehash function pinned; if mismatch detected rerun compute_bucket for affected tenant and run targeted correction job.

devin: final ask: measure query latency for canary tenants (tail latencies) and abort if p99 regresses >30% vs baseline.

maya: good guardrail. i'll author the RFC with perf numbers, backfill steps, adapter API contract, and rollout checklist. aiming to post RFC for review EOW.

alex: thanks — pls cc infra and console teams when RFC posted.

sarah: thumbs up :thumbsup:

maya: thanks everyone. posting draft in #eng-platform/rfc when ready.
